sketches.mechanism: The `object` declaration creates a singleton — exactly one instance, forever alone, that can never be instantiated again.
sketches.resonance: A declaration that there is only one of you in the entire runtime, and there will never be another.

sketches.mechanism: A weak reference does not keep the referenced object alive; once all strong references are gone, it silently becomes nil.
sketches.resonance: Holding someone weakly means you remember them, but your remembering alone cannot keep them from disappearing.

sketches.mechanism: Ownership transfer (move semantics) — assigning a value to someone else makes it inaccessible to you; using it afterward is a compile error.
sketches.resonance: After you give something away, trying to reach for it again is not just futile — the language itself refuses to let you pretend you still have it.
